analyst_observations: Both configurations achieve 100% pass rate on all assertions — the baseline agent had access to the full BESSER codebase and could research answers independently.

The key advantage of skills is EFFICIENCY: with-skill runs are consistently faster (35% mean speedup) and use fewer tokens (25% mean reduction). The agent doesn't need to explore the codebase since the skill provides the information directly.

The speedup is most pronounced on complex tasks: eval-3 (customization patterns) was 45% faster with skill, and eval-7 (adding a generator) was 21% faster. These are tasks where codebase exploration overhead is highest.
For simple diagnostics (eval-5, import error), the speed advantage is smaller (39%) because even without the skill, the answer is quick to find in the code.

Qualitatively, the with-skill responses are more CONCISE and CONSISTENT — they follow standardized patterns from the skill rather than discovering patterns by reading source code. The without-skill responses tend to include more raw file references and implementation details.

Non-discriminating assertions: All assertions pass in both configurations. For future iterations, consider adding assertions about response quality (conciseness, pattern consistency) rather than just correctness.
